acceptanceCriteria: Exactly one CURRENT operator note exists per ticket; superseded/cleared notes remain available through history.
Queue-derived timestamps and optional expected superseded revision prevent future-dated guidance and racing edits.
Ticket show and successful claim deliver current note with authority and freshness semantics; deterministic tests cover replacement, clear, conflicts and replay.
Required contract, independent review, focused qualification, CEM/OCM, current-main integration and native completion/readback/audit are retained.
body:
Owner-requested GitHub issue https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/issues/501; parallel execution requested 2026-10-03.

## Problem
Operator guidance to a ticket's next worker has no first-class channel. We prepend notes to the ticket's status file. Over a few days one ticket accumulated 9 stacked, partly contradictory operator notes ("owner must reopen" after reopen was refused; a 40-call cap beating an 80-call override). Workers burn their budget reading them, and some obey stale ones. One whole review session was lost this way.

## Request
`corvint-tasks ticket note set --target T --text ...` / `note clear` / `note show`, with these semantics:
- exactly one CURRENT note per ticket; setting a new one archives the old (still readable via history);
- shown in `ticket show` and in the claim result so the worker gets it without reading files;
- timestamped by the queue (never the caller), so notes cannot be future-dated (which workers distrusted twice);
- optional `supersedes` check against a revision to avoid racing edits.

## Workaround in use
`tools/fp-note.py`: archives all older top-of-file operator notes to an evidence file and writes one CURRENT line.
